title: Private deployment: regional residency & failover controls for data residency and evidence automation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a configurable control set for Private/VPC/on-prem customers to: 1) enforce regional data residency boundaries for storage (logs, KV caches, artifacts) and model artifacts, 2) provide retention policy configuration and automated deletion evidence, and 3) define regional failover constraints that prevent cross-region data movement except under operator-authorized scenarios. Deliverables include API/console controls, enforcement in the control plane agent, audit evidence generation, and an automated reporting job that produces monthly compliance packages.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can select permitted regions for persistent data (S3-compatible blob, DB, KV cache) at project and org level via API and Console
Retention policies (retain_for_days / purge_on_delete flags) can be configured per-data-class and enforced by the agent with automated deletion proofs (signed manifests)
Regional failover policy object supports: allowed_failover_regions (list), failover_mode (automatic/manual), and approved_excuse_ids (auditable override references)
Control plane agent enforces flows: any storage write/read across forbidden regions is blocked and logged; agent emits structured audit events to customer-owned audit sink

Monthly compliance report (PDF + machine-readable JSON) is generated for each org, containing residency snapshot, retention events (deletions with proofs), and failover incidents with justification links
End-to-end integration tests covering: residency violation blocked, retention purge proof, and failover event recorded and surfaced in Console
Security review completed and sign-off from Security and Legal on evidence format and retention of the report itself
updates: 2026-02-20: RFC drafted — outlined data-class taxonomy (logs, KV cache, model artifacts, customer blobs) and proposed enforcement points (agent, control plane, and storage policy). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Residency+Controls+RFC

2026-02-25: Design sync with PM and Security; decision to implement retention proofs as signed manifests produced by the control plane and anchored to a customer KMS key. Trade-off: increases agent complexity but simplifies downstream audits.

2026-03-02: Spike complete — prototype agent hook prevents cross-region writes using region allowlist; benchmark shows 3% median latency increase for metadata checks. Notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/spikes/ENG-4127-agent-spike
2026-03-05: Security review (initial) — requested schema for signed manifest and retention-proof lifecycle. Action: add manifest rotation policy and HSM support path.
2026-03-09: Implemented API changes for org.region_policy and project.retention_profile. Added OpenAPI spec changes in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/582

2026-03-11: Console mocks available for review in Figma: https://figma.redwood.ai/file/Private-Residency-Controls. PM feedback: expose quick override for emergency manual failover with mandatory justification link to an incident ticket.
2026-03-12: In-progress: building monthly report generator and wiring audit event sink to customer S3 in Private installs. Preparing integration test harness for on-prem environment.

qa_plan: Unit tests for region policy evaluation and manifest signer
Integration test in on-prem testbed: simulate disallowed-region write and validate block + audit event
E2E retention test: create artifacts, apply retention_policy=7d, run purge job, verify signed deletion manifest present in report
Failover test: trigger allowed_failover to secondary region in manual mode and verify audit trail and required justification is recorded
rollout_plan: Canary deploy control plane changes to staging Private cluster
Deploy agent update to a subset of customers with opt-in flag 'residency_beta'
Collect telemetry for 2 weeks (policy check latency, blocked write counts, retention-job success rate), then widen rollout
Provide migration guide and sample retention templates in Console and Docs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased request latency due to policy checks. Mitigation: per-connection TTL cache and batched policy updates.

Risk: Inconsistent enforcement across mixed-version agents. Mitigation: Control plane will run a compatibility check and refuse to apply residence policies to clusters with outdated agents; provide upgrade path.
Risk: Legal acceptance of signed manifests. Mitigation: Consult Legal early and include KMS-backed signing and nonce timestamps; provide human-readable proof export for auditors.

Risk: Emergency cross-region failovers needed for DR. Mitigation: implement manual override flow that logs justification and requires two operator approvals for customers with high residency constraints.
notes: Prefer using customer-owned audit sinks in Private installs to avoid duplicating sensitive evidence in Redwood-managed storage.
Consider later extension: automated SLA-triggered failover that only moves ephemeral caches and not persistent artifacts unless explicit override is granted.
Follow-up work: PM to coordinate pilot customers and Legal to validate report templates before GA.
